title: Supramolecular soft matter in traditional Chinese medicine: multiscale structure–function evidence, critical limitations, and translational challenges
abstract: Plant metabolites used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can form supramolecular assemblies in decoctions or in formulations prepared from purified molecules. These experimental settings support different conclusions. This narrative review examines TCM-derived supramolecular soft matter (TCM-derived SSM) through relationships among molecular interactions, assembly structure, physicochemical properties, and biological responses. It distinguishes assemblies isolated from decoctions, recombined extracts, formulations prepared from purified metabolites, and mixtures of defined metabolites with extracts. Micelles, vesicles, nanoparticles (NPs), nanofibers (NFs), and supramolecular gels provide examples, while carbonized products and covalently crosslinked carriers are discussed as related materials with distinct formation mechanisms. Selected studies associate morphology, surface chemistry, or deformability with altered delivery and preclinical activity. However, the presence of particles, successful reconstitution, and improved efficacy do not individually establish that an assembly is necessary for the effect of a complete preparation. Our contribution is an evidence-oriented comparison of preparation routes, structural measurements, biological comparisons, and the limits of inference across these preparations. We also examine artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted modeling and candidate critical quality attributes (CQAs) within a Quality by Design (QbD) perspective. Predictive design and assembly-based quality control are presented as research prospects that require reproducible measurements, appropriate controls, and validation across batches and biological settings. Self-assembly is a general physicochemical phenomenon; TCM provides a context for studying defined botanical drug combinations and preparation processes rather than evidence of properties unique to one medical tradition. We position this physical-state perspective within the established literature on synergy, antagonism and pharmacokinetic interactions in botanical mixtures.

title: From “Dual-Cluster Coexistence” to One-Dimensional Chains: Anion-Regulated Assembly of Copper(I)-Iodide Supramolecular Clusters for Enhanced Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract The self-assembly of ionic copper(I) iodide clusters is hard to control due to the diverse Cu–I coordination modes. We propose an electrostatically driven strategy to direct distinct architectures within the same ligand system by simply varying the counteranion. A cavitand-like ligand based on a triphenylamine pyridinium salt was designed. Solvothermal assembly with Br– and PF6– anions afforded two anionic supramolecular clusters:Br– induced the formation of an anionic cluster (denoted HUBU-4, [(L1)3+2·(Cu6Br1.47I7.53)3–]·(Cu5Br0.66I7.34)3–) featuring a “dual cluster coexistence” motif, whereas PF6– directed the formation of a one-dimensional cluster chain (HUBU-5, [(L1·PF6–)2+·(Cu5I7)2–]∞). DFT calculations and photophysical/electrochemical measurements show that HUBU-5 has a narrower optical band gap, a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, and stronger electronic transition capability than HUBU-4. (optical band gaps: 1.49 eV for HUBU-5 vs 1.62 eV for HUBU-4). Photocatalytic evaluation indicated that both clusters possess high activity for the copper(I)-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction under mild conditions, with a modest performance enhancement observed for the one-dimensional chain architecture. By simply changing the counteranion, this study achieves topological regulation of anionic copper(I) iodide clusters from 0D to 1D, revealing the structure-directing role of anions and offering an alternative design strategy for ionic supramolecular clusters.

title: Synergistic Spatial Confinement and Co-Reactant Acceleration Enable a Self-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence–Electrochemical Dual-Mode Aptasensor for Acetamiprid
abstract: Abstract A long electron transfer distance and significant energy dissipation could cause low electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency during mass-transfer reactions. To address this, a synergistic strategy based on spatial confinement and coreactant acceleration was proposed to enhance the ECL performance. Via an in situ self-assembly method, the luminophore (Ru(dcbpy)32+) and the coreactant (NGQDs) were simultaneously encapsulated within the zirconium imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) to form Ru-NGQDs@ZIF-8 composites. The porous structure of ZIF-8 confines both components, thereby shortening the electron-transfer pathway and reducing energy loss. Meanwhile, ZIF-8 itself also acts as a coreaction accelerator, which significantly enhances the ECL efficiency. On this basis, a self-enhanced ECL-electrochemical (EC) dual-mode aptasensor was developed for acetamiprid detection, exhibiting a linear range of 1 pM-100 nM and a low detection limit of 0.046 pM. This work develops a simple and efficient one-step synthesis method for self-enhanced ECL composites, and the constructed dual-mode aptasensor exhibits promising applications for the detection of acetamiprid.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Associated Bioactive Hydrogels: Material Roles, Network Design, and Therapeutic Applications
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-associated hydrogels are structurally diverse systems in which medicinal constituents can function primarily as gelators, cooperating network components, matrix-functionalizing moieties, scaffold-forming medicinal polysaccharides, or therapeutic payloads. This diversity expands formulation possibilities but can obscure the respective contributions of material design, delivery, and pharmacological activity. This review proposes a role-based framework that distinguishes constituent identity and chemical complexity from experimentally demonstrated network function. It applies this framework to active-molecule self-assembly, multicomponent and metal-assisted assembly, polymer-supported integration, medicinal-polysaccharide networks, and gel formulations containing complex herbal preparations. Therapeutic applications are considered in relation to four recurring pathological and delivery constraints, including limited residence at dynamic interfaces, oxidative and inflammatory microenvironments, structurally deficient regenerative niches, and the need for spatial confinement when systemic or off-target exposure constrains treatments. Across these applications, this review assesses evidence for hydrated-network formation, component-resolved release and exposure, and appropriate comparators, while distinguishing structural cooperation from coordinated delivery and pharmacological synergy. Future progress will require reproducible feedstocks and processing, physiologically relevant characterization, manufacturing-aware design, and standardized datasets to support predictive modeling. This review provides a conceptual roadmap for the development and utilization of TCM-associated hydrogels as bioactive biomaterials.
